source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 5 (Legislature).

sections.heading: 1. Why We Need a Parliament
points: The **legislature (Parliament)** makes laws, controls the executive, holds the purse, and is a forum of debate and representation.
India has a **bicameral Parliament**: **Lok Sabha (House of the People, lower house)** and **Rajya Sabha (Council of States, upper house)** + the President.

sections.heading: 2. Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
points: **Lok Sabha** — **directly elected** by people; max strength 550 (+ earlier 2 Anglo-Indian nominated, now discontinued); term **5 years** (can be dissolved); presided by the **Speaker**.

**Rajya Sabha** — **indirectly elected** (by state assemblies via STV) + 12 nominated by President; a **permanent house** (not dissolved; one-third retire every 2 years, 6-year terms); chaired by the **Vice-President**.
**Money Bills** can be introduced **only in the Lok Sabha**; Rajya Sabha has limited power over them (can only delay 14 days).

sections.heading: 3. Law-Making and Control
points: A **bill** passes through: introduction (first reading), general discussion + committee (second reading), voting (third reading), then the other house, then President's assent.
**Money Bills** vs **Ordinary Bills** vs **Constitutional Amendment Bills** differ in procedure.
Parliament controls the executive via: **question hour, zero hour, motions (no-confidence, adjournment, censure), and committees**.
The Lok Sabha is more powerful in financial matters and in removing the government (no-confidence).

sections.heading: 4. Anti-Defection and Committees
points: The **Anti-Defection Law (52nd Amendment, 1985 — Tenth Schedule)** disqualifies legislators who defect; decided by the presiding officer.
**Parliamentary committees** (standing, ad hoc, financial) do detailed scrutiny of bills, budgets and administration (e.g. Public Accounts Committee, Estimates Committee).
Committees compensate for the limited time in the full house.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Parliament = Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha + President.
Lok Sabha = directly elected (5 yrs, Speaker); Rajya Sabha = indirectly elected (permanent, Vice-President chairs).
Money Bills only in Lok Sabha; Rajya Sabha can delay only 14 days.
Anti-Defection Law = 52nd Amendment (1985), Tenth Schedule.
No-confidence motion is moved only in the Lok Sabha.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha** (Rajya Sabha's power is limited).
**Rajya Sabha is a permanent house** (never fully dissolved); one-third retire every 2 years.
The **Speaker** presides over the Lok Sabha; the **Vice-President** chairs the Rajya Sabha.
The **Anti-Defection Law** is in the **Tenth Schedule (52nd Amendment, 1985)**.
